nodes.label: A woman in her 60s presented with a new pruritic rash involving the legs, feet, arms, hands, and trunk
The rash initially developed on the legs 13 days before presentation, then progressed to the feet, arms, hands, and trunk, with associated burning sensation and occasional pain.

Medical history included endometrial adenocarcinoma status post hysterectomy and recent postoperative radiotherapy totaling 50.4 Gy in 28 fractioned doses, completed 4 days after rash onset; she denied new medications, chemotherapy, intravenous contrast exposure, or recent travel.

Physical examination showed numerous erythematous edematous coalescing papules and plaques on the upper and lower extremities, scattered erythematous papules and plaques on the back and buttocks, some plaques annular and polycyclic with central hyperpigmentation, while the chest, abdomen, face, and oral mucosa were clear.
Skin biopsy reveals numerous eosinophils without leukocytoclasia
Radiotherapy field mapping was not retrieved, so spatial correlation cannot be confirmed
Rash is widespread beyond the radiation treatment field
Flame figures were not confirmed on biopsy
